transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-08
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Tomás Rivera (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Ironclad Head of ML), Ben Kline (Platform), Sana Rahman (SRE)

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route usage topology, how to slice cost by customer routes, and mapping usage to SLOs. Customer wants to understand whether Dedicated or Hosted makes sense given bursty traffic and strict PII rules.

Topics covered: console overview, per-route dashboards, cost-slicing, batching + KV cache impact, routing policies, security (SSO/SAML, KMS), next steps and benchmarks.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alicia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Can you all hear me okay?
[00:05] Maya Chen: Yep, loud and clear.
[00:07] Ben Kline: Good here.
[00:09] Alicia Park: Great. Quick introductions, I'm Alicia, AE on Redwood inference, and Tomás is our SE who will walk through the Console.
[00:14] Tomás Rivera: Hi all. I'll mainly show dashboards and then dig into how route-level cost is calculated and how batching and KV cache change the numbers.
[00:21] Maya Chen: Perfect. To set context: Ironclad's using a mix of internal and customer-facing models. We have latency SLOs of 200 ms p95 for customer-facing, and some internal jobs can be async. We're trying to figure out if we go Hosted first or move to Dedicated pools — also need to keep data residency and KMS in mind.
[00:36] Alicia Park: Thanks. Short agenda: console tour focused on usage topology and cost-slicing, then a quick Q&A about security and deployment options, end with next steps.
[00:45] Tomás Rivera: Opening the Console. (brief pause) Okay, first screen is the overall usage lens — you'll see tokens, calls, and errors across your org. The important bit for this call is Routes.
[00:58] [00:58] Tomás Rivera: Switching to the Routes view — this shows each logical route you define, along with throughput, avg latency, and cost per route. Note that cost is a synthesized number: token cost + per-request overhead + GPU time estimate.
[01:12] Sana Rahman: Sorry — when you say per-request overhead, is that network or infra?
[01:16] Tomás Rivera: Good question — it's a small fixed amortized overhead we attach to each request to cover orchestration and vcpu usage, yes. It's configurable if you allocate Dedicated and pin capacity.
[01:26] Maya Chen: Can we change the cost model? Our finance team wants to see chargebacks by product team.
[01:30] Tomás Rivera: Absolutely. You can export per-route token counts and set custom per-token rates in the Console, or use our API to pull route-level metrics and then map them in your billing system. We'll show exports in a sec.
[01:40] [01:40] Tomás Rivera: Now I want to show an example — I'm toggling a 'batching on' profile. See how the per-route cost drops in the left panel? That's because batching increases GPU throughput and reduces time per token. The Console estimates batching efficiency based on observed sequence length distributions.
[01:58] Ben Kline: Is that the same place where you show the KV cache hit rate?
[02:02] Tomás Rivera: Right after this. KV (K-V) cache hit rate is visible per route. If your route uses system prompts that repeat, we often see big wins. Note the hit rate gauge — higher hit rate reduces effective token counts.
[02:16] Maya Chen: A lot of our calls are short but frequent — does batching help or hurt latency?
[02:21] Tomás Rivera: There's a trade-off. Console shows expected p95 impact per route when you enable batching at various thresholds. For short, high-QPS routes batching may add a small tail-latency penalty; we show both cost delta and latency delta so you can pick an SLO-aware plan.
[02:36] [02:36] Tomás Rivera: Now, here's the topology map — this is useful: it groups routes by service, highlights cross-route KV reuse, and surfaces the top 10 routes that drive tokens. In your case, if your auth route is hitting the model for every session, that will show up as a hotspot.
[02:48] Maya Chen: Our auth used to ping the model for contextual enrollment, yeah. We did some caching on our side but could be better.
[02:54] Alicia Park: For data residency, you mentioned KMS earlier — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem control plane. We have a short security pack I'll send.
[03:03] Sana Rahman: We need to know about HSM or key isolation for certain routes that touch PII. Can Dedicated help with that?
[03:10] Tomás Rivera: Yes, Dedicated + Private deployment options give you more control. We can map an encryption policy per route so that audit logs for those routes are retained separately and keys are customer-controlled. We'll schedule security deep-dive for that.
[03:21] [03:21] Tomás Rivera: Back to the Console — I want to show cost-slicing. Picking three example routes: customer-chat, internal-embed, and search-rerank. In the export CSV you'll get tokens_by_route, calls_by_route, avg_seq_len, kv_hit, and an estimated GPU-ms.
[03:36] Ben Kline: Does GPU-ms come from telemetry or from model profile?
[03:40] Tomás Rivera: It's modeled — we combine model performance profiles with observed sequence lengths and batching efficiency to estimate GPU-ms. For Dedicated, we refine that with real GPU telemetry.
[03:47] Maya Chen: If we wanted to do chargeback, could we attach tags to routes so the Console groups by team or product?
[03:53] Tomás Rivera: Yes — tags are first-class. You can tag routes with product, team, environment, and Console will aggregate cost by tag. You can then slice dashboards or export.
[04:01] [04:01] Tomás Rivera: Another thing — canaries and rollout policies: if you have an expensive model, Console can route a percentage of traffic to an exec variant while keeping the cheaper fallback. That shows up in route economics as blended cost.
[04:12] Maya Chen: That blended view would be super helpful. We often run A/Bs and then our finance folks are confused by the blended cost.
[04:18] Tomás Rivera: We also have a timeline view, you can select the rollout window and Console will recompute blended costs for that period.
[04:24] [04:24] Ben Kline: Small question on accuracy — when you estimate cost for hosted vs dedicated, how close is it to real bills?
[04:29] Tomás Rivera: For hosted, cost is pretty close to what you'll see on your invoice because we use the same unit pricing. For Dedicated, Console models amortized GPU cost and committed capacity; we show committed vs burst delta. When you accept reserved capacity, the modeled cost will show lower per-token but fixed monthly.
[04:42] Maya Chen: Our traffic is very spiky — we get big bursts twice a day. How does Console show burst cost?
[04:47] Tomás Rivera: There's a burst-cost analysis. It shows how many minutes you spend in burst mode above baseline capacity and suggests either increasing baseline or enabling burst credits. The Optimize recommendations page will even suggest quantization or model variant swaps for burst windows.
[04:59] [04:59] Tomás Rivera: I'm going to open the exports menu — here's a quick CSV preview. You can push this to S3 or fetch via API. Alicia, can you remind them about the shared sandbox?
[05:08] Alicia Park: Sure — we'll provision a sandbox org with sample data and a pre-configured dashboard for Ironclad. We'll also include a small spreadsheet that maps exported columns to common chargeback formats.
[05:17] Maya Chen: Great, that helps.
[05:20] [05:20] Sana Rahman: Two security items — audit logs retention and SSO. How long are logs retained and can we forward to our Splunk?
[05:26] Tomás Rivera: Audit logs are retained per your plan; we can forward logs to your SIEM (Splunk) and also support SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. We'll include the SSO integration guide in the security packet.
[05:37] Maya Chen: Do you provide SOC 2 artifacts?
[05:39] Alicia Park: Yes, we have a SOC 2 report and can share an overview; for deeper exchanges we'll need an NDA/MSA.
[05:45] [05:45] Ben Kline: Okay could we talk about latencies for quantized models? If we quantize to int8, what's the expected p95 impact?
[05:51] Tomás Rivera: Quantization often increases throughput and reduces GPU-ms, but you should validate quality. Console's Optimize tab will suggest quantization profiles per model and estimate the latency delta; typically p95 improves for larger context windows but single-token latency may change slightly. We'll run a short regression test in the sandbox if you'd like.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Yes please.
[06:09] [06:09] Tomás Rivera: Alright — quick demo of a customer scenario: I mocked up Ironclad's top 5 routes in the sandbox. See here: customer-chat is 48% of tokens, but rerank is 30% of GPU-ms because rerank uses long contexts. Console suggests enabling prefix KV for chat and batching for rerank which reduces overall cost by an estimated 27%.
[06:28] Maya Chen: 27% is significant. Is that mostly from batching?
[06:32] Tomás Rivera: It's batching + cache + swapping an LLM variant for rerank in non-critical windows. The recommendation shows per-route estimated savings and a confidence score.
[06:41] [06:41] Alicia Park: Quick note — we'll need your real traffic if you want exact estimates. The Sandbox uses model averages.
[06:47] Maya Chen: Sure, I'll send the CSV.
[06:49] [06:49] Tomás Rivera: Final callouts: alerts. You can create an alert when per-route cost exceeds X or when latency breaches SLO. The Runbooks link triggers a fallback policy — e.g., route falls back to smaller model or to cached response.
[07:02] Ben Kline: Would fallback be automatic? We don't want to silently degrade quality.
[07:05] Tomás Rivera: It's configurable — you can have an automatic fallback with an approval gate or manual notification. The Console logs both pre- and post-fallback outputs for auditing.
[07:15] [07:15] Maya Chen: Ok, timeline and next steps for us? We are aiming to decide by end of next quarter.
[07:20] Alicia Park: Proposed cadence: sandbox/benchmark this week, security deep-dive next week, then pilot (4–6 weeks) to validate cost/sla before Q3 commit.
[07:30] Maya Chen: That works.
[07:32] [07:32] Tomás Rivera: I'll follow up with a runbook for the benchmark. For the 1-hour run we need top payloads and a representative seq length distribution.
[07:41] Sana Rahman: We'll also want to see how audit logs are separated per route in Dedicated.
[07:45] Alicia Park: Noted — Tomás will prep the security snippets.
[07:48] [07:48] (small cross talk)
[07:50] Maya Chen: One last question — if we start Hosted and later move to Dedicated, how disruptive is it?
[07:55] Tomás Rivera: Low disruption — same API and routes. You pin model versions and traffic shifts are handled by the routing policy. Console will show both org-level and env-level comparisons so you can validate. Migration playbook has steps and rollback.
[08:09] Maya Chen: That's reassuring.
[08:11] Alicia Park: Okay wrapping up — I'll send the recording, the deck, the sandbox invite, and the security pack. Tomás will kick off the perf run once Maya shares the CSV. We'll also schedule a 60-minute security deep-dive with our Security PM — is next Wednesday OK?
[08:25] Maya Chen: Next Wednesday works.
[08:27] Ben Kline: Works for me.
[08:29] Sana Rahman: OK.
[08:31] Alicia Park: Great — thanks everyone. We'll be in touch and track action items in the email thread.
[08:36] Maya Chen: Thank you.
[08:37] Ben Kline: Thanks.
[08:38] Tomás Rivera: Thanks all.

--- End transcript ---
